scope.edition: Classic English base game (1996), Jay Tummelson translation/editing
scope.includes: All base Action Card explanations in stacks 1–5
scope.verdict_basis: Material gameplay accuracy, important omissions, timing, origins/destinations, quantities/costs, exceptions and ending. Administrative verification-banner/history claims are not game rules and were not independently adjudicated.

conclusion: No material rule error or important gameplay omission found. The rules body matches the complete in-scope publisher source, and the summary expressly discloses the principal source contradictions and missing procedures rather than inventing definitive resolutions.

checked_claims.claim: Edition, players, components and action-stack composition
checked_claims.source_reference: PDF pp.1–3
checked_claims.assessment: Supported. Classic 1996 base game, 2–5 players, 31 cubes per color including the score marker, 13 power cards per player, 11 action cards per stacks 1–4 and one King card.

checked_claims.source_reference: PDF pp.2–3, Preparation and Playing the Game
checked_claims.assessment: Supported. King and home regions come from separate drawn region cards; each player starts with two board Caballeros, seven court Caballeros and one scoring marker. Disks exclude Castillo; mobile scoreboards begin beside the board; standard round marker starts at 1.

checked_claims.claim: Round sequence, power-card bidding and turn order
checked_claims.source_reference: PDF pp.3–4
checked_claims.assessment: Supported. Five cards revealed; first starter chosen, subsequently previous round last-turn player starts; clockwise power play with unique values; descending-value turns; only top used power card visible; unused actions discarded and King card reused.

checked_claims.source_reference: PDF p.3, Player turns step 1; p.4, taboo; p.7(A),(C)
checked_claims.assessment: Supported. Recruitment is at most the power-card allowance, before choosing the action card. Own board pieces may make up a provinces shortage; King region and Castillo remain protected.
Supported. At most the action-card allowance from court, divided among regions adjacent to current King and Castillo. King movement before deployment changes the adjacency test.

checked_claims.source_reference: PDF pp.3–4; p.7(D),(G)
checked_claims.assessment: Supported. Deployment and special action may occur in either order, each must be completed before starting the other, and special action may be declined. Chosen action becomes unavailable to later players.

Supported. No Caballero, Grande or mobile scoreboard enters/leaves King region; King itself may move. Castillo can receive Caballeros irrespective of King location; arrivals announced; contents leave only at general scoring.

checked_claims.claim: Stack 1: all-own-region, extra court pieces, either/or choice
checked_claims.source_reference: PDF p.8, first three Intrigue explanations; p.7
checked_claims.assessment: Supported. Whole own group may be redistributed with some returned to origin; two extra court pieces have unrestricted non-King destinations; combined card chooses one special effect.

checked_claims.claim: Stack 1: five from one origin and three-piece effects
checked_claims.source_reference: PDF p.8, five-Caballero and three-Caballero Intrigue explanations
checked_claims.assessment: Supported. Five-piece effect has one origin and mixed ownership; three-foreign effect excludes own pieces; unrestricted three allows mixed ownership and multiple origins. General taboo and Castillo restrictions retained.

checked_claims.source_reference: PDF p.8, final three Intrigue explanations; p.7(E)
checked_claims.assessment: Supported. Two-own and two-foreign allowances are distinct; four-own effect excludes foreign pieces; other four-piece effect permits mixed ownership. All nine unique Stack 1 descriptions are covered, including both duplicate card types.

checked_claims.claim: Stack 2: veto duration, target and partial execution
checked_claims.source_reference: PDF p.9, Veto explanation
checked_claims.assessment: Supported. Veto acts once on an incomplete special action, not ordinary placement; announcement and stopping remainder are covered; completed portions are not undone; unused card expires end of following round.

checked_claims.claim: Stack 2: court decay and King returns
checked_claims.source_reference: PDF p.9, Decay of Authority and The King returns explanations/card faces
checked_claims.assessment: Supported. Decay affects fellow players and has explicit all-remaining treatment for fewer than three court pieces. King returns follows detailed each-player paragraph and matching card, clockwise from selecting player left, with selecting player included; heading conflict and missing shortfall procedure are disclosed.

checked_claims.source_reference: PDF p.9, You send 1 Caballero explanation
checked_claims.assessment: Supported. Selecting player chooses one board-region piece from each player including self, returned to provinces; court, King region and Castillo are not permitted sources. No unsupported shortfall resolution added.

checked_claims.source_reference: PDF p.9, remove-two explanation/card; p.10, remove-all explanation/card; p.7(A),(B),(C)
checked_claims.assessment: Supported with disclosed source limitations. One secret origin per affected player, simultaneous disk choice, correct ownership/destinations and one-piece fallback for remove-two; no-piece exception for remove-all; protected origins remain excluded. Summary identifies the all-players versus fellow-players wording conflict rather than silently resolving it.

checked_claims.source_reference: PDF p.10, Special Scoring: pick one region; pp.5–6; p.7(C)
checked_claims.assessment: Supported. Any region including King region or Castillo, normal scoring and bonuses; Castillo contents are not distributed.

checked_claims.claim: Stack 3: value categories and mobile scoreboard replacement
checked_claims.source_reference: PDF p.10, all-4, all-5, all-6/7 explanations
checked_claims.assessment: Supported. Category uses current first-place value, all nine printed regional values match, mobile boards change category membership, and all-5 effect excludes Castillo explicitly.

checked_claims.source_reference: PDF pp.10–11, Castillo and choose-any-region explanations
checked_claims.assessment: Supported. Castillo is uncovered, scored and re-covered with the same pieces; chosen-region card may choose King region or Castillo.

checked_claims.source_reference: PDF p.11, corresponding special-scoring explanations
checked_claims.assessment: Supported. First-only gives nothing for tied first; most/least score every tied qualifying region; Castillo excluded; least also excludes empty regions. All eight unique Stack 3 descriptions are present.

checked_claims.claim: Stack 4: mobile scoreboard and Royal Adviser
checked_claims.source_reference: PDF p.11, corresponding explanations
checked_claims.assessment: Supported. Mobile board may enter or relocate, including Castillo; taboo, no stacking and printed orientations retained. Royal Adviser moves King only one neighboring region.

checked_claims.source_reference: PDF p.11, Movement; p.7(A)–(C)
checked_claims.assessment: Supported. Only fellow players move their entire group from selected region; disks simultaneous; choosing King region or original region returns pieces to court. Does not invent access to protected sources.

checked_claims.claim: Stack 4: Grande movement and home-region change
checked_claims.source_reference: PDF p.12, Grande explanation
checked_claims.assessment: Supported. Own Grande, non-King/non-Castillo destination, cannot leave King region, multiple Grandes at destination allowed; new location becomes home region.

checked_claims.claim: Stack 4: recovered power card, Court and unique disk scoring
checked_claims.source_reference: PDF p.12, corresponding explanations; p.7(D)
checked_claims.assessment: Supported. Any one used power card including current turn can return unrevealed; Court brings two own provinces pieces to court; all players choose scoring disks simultaneously and duplicated choices do not score. All seven unique Stack 4 descriptions are present.

checked_claims.source_reference: PDF p.12, Action cards in the 5 stack; pp.4,7
checked_claims.assessment: Supported. Up to five ordinary deployments plus optional King movement to any region except Castillo; King location at deployment time controls adjacency.

checked_claims.claim: General scoring schedule, information timing and destinations
checked_claims.source_reference: PDF pp.3,5
checked_claims.assessment: Supported. After rounds 3,6,9, select secret destinations before uncovering; score Castillo; reveal disks and move each player whole Castillo group to one region, or court if King region selected; replace empty Castillo; then score all board regions in track order.

checked_claims.source_reference: PDF pp.5–6, Scoring of the Regions and both examples
checked_claims.assessment: Supported. Grandes do not count. Only first pays with two players, first two with three. Tied group drops one paid rank regardless of group size; lower group follows paid rank, matching explicit three-way-first example. Third-place tie scores zero; two-player tie falls beyond payable rank.

checked_claims.source_reference: PDF p.6, King bonus and Home region bonus; p.10, all-4 scoring
checked_claims.assessment: Supported. Each bonus is +2 for sole majority; own Grande required for home bonus; no bonus on first-place tie; applicable during special scoring as well as general scoring.

checked_claims.source_reference: PDF p.6, Game End; p.5, general scoring sequence
checked_claims.assessment: Supported. Finish third general scoring including regions, then furthest along success track wins. No invented final tiebreaker.

checked_claims.source_reference: PDF pp.1–12 in full
checked_claims.assessment: No material gameplay omission identified. Every unique base Action Card explanation is represented, with duplicate card effects consolidated. No added resource costs, altered destinations, extra scoring round, edition changes, expansion rules or optional short-game procedure identified. Source conflicts are disclosed; no compulsory fallback procedure is invented for unclear returns.

source_limitations.source_reference: PDF p.9, The King returns heading, card face and explanation
source_limitations.description: Heading says fellow players, but card face and detailed clockwise execution paragraph say each player. Summary expressly identifies conflict and follows the detailed paragraph plus matching card face; this is a disclosed reading, not an independently verified publisher clarification.

Card faces/headings affect fellow players; explanatory text says all players select disks. Source does not reconcile selecting player participation. Summary preserves that gap and does not silently require selecting player removal.

source_limitations.source_reference: PDF p.9, The King returns and remove-two; p.10, remove-all; p.7(A),(C)
source_limitations.description: Source does not supply complete legal disk/shortfall procedures for fewer than three eligible King-returns pieces, no eligible remove-two origin, or pieces only in protected King region. The remove-all text exempts players with no pieces in any region, but does not explicitly address pieces only in King region. Summary does not authorize protected removal or invent a definitive fallback.

source_limitations.source_reference: PDF p.9, one-per-player return; p.12, The Court
source_limitations.description: Source gives no explicit fallback when a player has no eligible piece for the one-per-player return or provinces cannot supply both Court pieces. Summary repeats the stated effects without adding an unsupported remedy.
No additional endgame tiebreaker is provided. Summary correctly records the absence rather than inventing one.

source_limitations.source_reference: PDF p.10, category special scorings; p.11, mobile scoreboard
source_limitations.description: Source explicitly excludes Castillo for all-5 scoring but does not separately discuss all-4 scoring when the 4/0/0 mobile scoreboard is on Castillo. Summary states the general current-value rule without inventing a categorical Castillo exclusion for all-4.

PDF text extraction has interleaved card-face/illustration labels and excessive layout spacing. The complete supplied extraction and direct PDF text were both read, including normalized PDF text around the conflicting card faces. No external editions, FAQs, expansions or optional short-game rules were used.

non_rule_observations.observation: The 60–120 min frontmatter is a broad game-duration estimate. Publisher p.2 associates about two hours with nine rounds and about one hour with the optional six-round game excluded by this summary. Using approximately 120 min would align metadata more closely with the stated standard-game scope; this does not alter any gameplay rule or the audit verdict.
